newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Aussie stuck in a rut until rates resolved.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Aussie stuck in a rut until rates resolved.

text.p: *AUD starts its third week in the $0.7310/7440 range and looks to be heading nowhere while risk of rate cut lingers
*Resilience of support under $0.7330 and failure of short covering bounce at $0.7420 Friday re-confirmed strength of band
*Market betting on RBA rate cut after August 5 board meeting
*Among data due, retail sales Thursday to be most important
By 8.15 am (2215 GMT) the currency found itself in limbo at US$0.7374/79 having eased back from US$0.7404/09 late Friday.

It had rallied over 1/2 cent after the Reserve Bank confounded market speculation by not easing policy that morning but the short covering petered out around US$0.7420. Traders said the market still confidently expected the bank to cut rates for a fifth time and was now assuming it would do so after its monthly board meeting on August 5.
A 50 basis point easing to 5.0 percent was fully discounted by the futures market and the resilience of support last week suggested it was largely priced into the dollar as well.

They emphasised it was impossible to be sure offshore investors would be so sanguine if the expectation of lower rates became reality -- the five cent loss suffered since the last cut on May 23 proved that.

But bulls hoped some of those losses reflected the expectation of another easing and the dollar could enjoy a rally on the actual fact. This scenario also depended on any cut being seen as the last in the cycle and while analysts felt it probably would be, they cautioned nothing could be ruled out if the real side data remained weak.
Data due this week were expected to be middle of the road.

Retail trade on Thursday would be important as consumer spending, and confidence readings for that matter, have been noteably volatile this year. Median forecasts are for a modest 0.4 percent rise in June but this would be a firm result given it came on top of a 2.9 percent gain in May. Real sales for Q2, however, were to expected to show a marginal 0.1 percent rise after a 2.2 percent increase in Q1.

Elsewhere, the dollar remained strong on a number of crosses after the mark and Swiss franc haemorrhaged funds last week which in turn kept it relatively firm in trade weighted terms despite its losses against the US$. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
